about: The epistola of the formulary “Saint Matthias the Apostle” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: In those days, Peter, standing up among the brethren — now there was a crowd of people together, about one hundred twenty — said: Men, brethren, it is necessary that the Scripture be fulfilled which was spoken beforehand by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of David about Judas, who was the leader of those who seized Jesus; who had been counted among us, and received the lot of this ministry. And this man indeed possessed a field from the reward of iniquity, and, having been hanged, burst open in the middle, and all his entrails were poured out. And this became known to all who lived in Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their tongue Aceldama, which means, the field of blood. In the book of Psalms, indeed, it is written: Let their abode become deserted, and let there be no one to dwell in it; and let another take his bishopric. It is necessary, then, that from these men who have assembled with us all the time in which the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day on which He was taken up from us, one of these become with us a witness of His resurrection. So they proposed two: Joseph, who was called Barsabas, who bore the surname Justus, and Matthias. And praying, they said: Lord, You who know every heart, make known which one You have chosen of these two to receive the place of this ministry and of the apostleship, from which Judas turned aside through transgression, to depart to his own place. Then they gave them lots, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.
